body:
## Research findings that change this design: git records NO renames; newest-resolution is a view

Two Cluster-2 findings reshape the versioning design:

- **Git rename detection is a per-diff re-guess, not recorded lineage.** Git stores snapshots; rename detection runs heuristically at diff time (exact matches → same-basename pre-pass → pairwise similarity, **default threshold 50%**, `-M50%`; copies need `-C`). Documented failure modes: rename + heavy edit in one commit drops under threshold (reads as delete+create); file splits/merges are invisible to whole-file similarity; large diffs silently hit the rename limit. Drew's instinct — rename-only commits, `git mv`, no simultaneous edit — makes git lineage a **convention-dependent hint**, and this design may set that commit discipline for our repos, but **Atlas must compute and store its own lineage edges** (via segment search / the dedup-edge pipeline) as first-class data, with git's `-M` output as one input signal. Non-git sources (chats, logs, session stores) have no git signal at all — another reason the lineage graph lives in Atlas's tables.
- **"Take the max" must be a query-time view, not a destructive replace.** Delta/Iceberg time travel works because resolution happens at read. Newest-version resolution = a view over the lineage graph (per logical file: the version reachable from the current head edge), with explicit handling for deleted files (head = tombstone — the previous version does *not* resurface) and renamed paths (identity follows the lineage edge, not the path string). Destructive replacement would break the query-trace design ([#6027](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/6027)): a served result must forever resolve to the exact embed state that was served. Related dead end, recorded in a child below: Turso PITR is whole-DB disaster recovery (≤90-day windows) — never a corpus-retention mechanism.

### Wave-2 children filed under this issue

- [#6041](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/6041) — composite age/supersede/last-surfaced policy with a **dry-run reporter** (no silent vacuum)
- [#6042](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/6042) — self-describing rustfs shards + restore path
- [#6043](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/6043) — the layer-separation record


— Wave-2 research fold-in, 2026-11-04 (prior-art doc: `~/workspace/scratch/atlas-ingestion-brief-2026-11-04/prior-art-research.md`)

## Triage result — #6026

- **Scope:** this is a design issue, not a current runtime defect. No reproduction or code change is applicable. The issue remains OPEN; no related PR or existing Atlas versioning design doc was found on current main.
- **Research already on the issue:** Git rename detection is heuristic, so Atlas needs first-class lineage edges; newest-resolution should be a query-time view; wave-2 children #6041 (retention rule engine/dry-run), #6042 (cold-tier shard/restore), and #6043 (layer separation) are already filed.
- **Ordering:** use #3125 occurrence/provenance semantics for version-to-chunk lineage; coordinate query-time latest/as-of behavior with #5755/#5774 and retrieval statistics/query traces in #6027; fold #6041–#6043 into the parent design rather than opening duplicate tickets. The parent tracker #6018 is OPEN/parked and remains the source for broader Atlas scope.
- **Policy gate:** reconcile this design with #3125’s keep-all rule. Default to retain unless both a class rule and explicit trigger allow retirement; deletion must not orphan chunk occurrences. Cold versions remain resolvable until deletion. The #6018 spend ceiling remains in force; any design option exceeding it needs Drew’s explicit approval, but no spend change is needed to complete the design.
- **Routing:** ready for the design stage; no separate queue packet was created because #6026 is already the design handoff and the research children are linked.

- **What landed:** only the PITR-vs-retention boundary decision — PR #6269 (merged 2026-11-05) added `doc/2026-11-05T15-50-41Z_decision_atlas_pitr_vs_retention/` and closed sibling issue #6043. It does not write the versioning design.

The version object model, lineage rules, per-class retention table with the three triggers (by date / by increments / by access), cold-rollout mechanics, and the query-side newest-resolution contract from issue #6026's "Done looks like" are all still unwritten.
- **Settled inputs (do not re-litigate):** the research comment on issue #6026 (git records no renames — lineage edges are Atlas-computed, git `-M` is one signal; newest-resolution is a query-time view with tombstone handling), the #3125 keep-all reconciliation rule (default keep unless a trigger AND a class rule both say retire; deletion never orphans chunk occurrences), and the PITR boundary from PR #6269.
